page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 1919 GB of local SSD storage, coupled with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The processor supports AVX and AVX-512f instructions, but lacks newer extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI or AMX.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.i2.2xlarge delivers modest processing capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier. Memory read bandwidth is also relatively low, with small block cached reads at 328.53 GB/sec and large block uncached reads at 39.23 GB/sec. However, large block memory write performance is average at 35.45 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance of 6.06 million operations per second are positioned in the weak category, while LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model remain average, processing 442.93 prompt tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is the combination of high-capacity local SSD storage and dedicated memory against lower-tier CPU compute performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2.2xlarge offers high local storage density and a generous memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it suitable for workloads that are storage-bound rather than compute-intensive. It is best suited for relational databases, NoSQL transactional stores, caching layers, and moderate data processing tasks that benefit from local SSD speeds and 64 GB of RAM but do not require high-frequency CPU performance.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it supports AVX and AVX-512f instructions. Benchmark results place its CPU and memory read performance in the lower 25% tier, though memory write speeds and small-model LLM inference remain average. The instance presents a clear tradeoff, offering high local storage capacity and a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio at the expense of raw computational speed. This profile makes the ecs.i2.2xlarge qualitatively cost-effective for storage-heavy and memory-dependent workloads rather than compute-intensive tasks. It is best suited for databases, caching systems, and localized data storage applications.
